tools.name: whoami
tools.description: The signed-in Alama account: username, display name and how many items and outfits it holds.

tools.name: get_context
tools.description: Start here. One bounded summary of the signed-in person: their wardrobe in numbers (garments per class, main colours, materials, formality) with the garments they use most, their written style profile, what the wardrobe is missing, their usual sizes, what they have recently worn, liked or rejected,

tools.name: style_profile
tools.description: The signed-in person's style profile as Alama has written it from their wardrobe and what they wear: a short summary, one line each on palette, shapes, formality, materials and most-worn pieces, their style words, what they avoid and their usual sizes. Use it to answer 'what do you know about my sty

tools.name: list_wardrobe
tools.description: The signed-in person's own clothes, most recently updated first, with category, colour, size, material, formality and warmth. Filter by category: a garment class ('tops', 'bottoms', 'dresses', 'outerwear', 'shoes', 'bags', 'hats', 'accessories') finds every item of that kind whatever its category is

tools.name: get_item
tools.description: One item from the signed-in person's wardrobe by id, with a one-hour link to its picture. An item without a photo comes with `add_photo_url` instead: a one-hour link where the person adds one.

tools.name: suggest_outfit
tools.description: Put together one outfit from the signed-in person's own clothes for an occasion, the weather or a date. Returns the chosen items with pictures and a short rationale. Nothing is saved. Free accounts get a daily allowance; Organiser and Style Pass are unlimited.

tools.name: does_it_suit_me
tools.description: Whether a product the person is looking at suits them, judged against their own wardrobe and style profile. Pass the product page link, a link to its picture, or its description (pass the description too when you have it: some shops refuse to show their pages to servers). Returns a verdict (suits yo

tools.name: wardrobe_gaps
tools.description: The core garment classes the signed-in person's wardrobe owns none of (for example footwear), plus how many items they own per class. Use it before recommending anything to buy.

tools.name: create_saved_outfit
tools.description: Save an outfit to the signed-in person's wardrobe from item ids they own, typically the ids suggest_outfit just returned. Give it a short name (e.g. 'Client dinner'). Works only once the person has turned on 'Allow assistants to change my wardrobe' under Profile → Connected assistants in the Alama a

tools.name: add_want
tools.description: Record that the signed-in person wants an outside product, usually right after does_it_suit_me. Pass the product page link, a link to its picture, or its description (pass the description too when you have it), and an optional short note. The product is described in the person's own wardrobe terms a

tools.name: record_signal
tools.description: Record one thing the signed-in person tells you, so their style profile learns from it: 'wore' (a garment they own, by item_id from list_wardrobe), 'bought', 'liked' or 'rejected' (a garment they own by item_id, or an outside product by its link or description). `on` is the day it happened, YYYY-MM-

tools.name: add_item
tools.description: Add one item the signed-in person says they own to their wardrobe, from its description (for example 'navy wool coat') or the link to its product page. One call per item. It is filed in Alama's own terms and returned as filed: read `reads_as` back so the person can correct it. The item has no photo

tools.name: list_saved_outfits
tools.description: The outfits the signed-in person has saved in Alama, most recently changed first, each with its `outfit_id`, its name and the items in it. Use it when they refer to an outfit they already have ('my Friday outfit', 'the look I saved last week'), or before try_on to find the `outfit_id`. `query` match

tools.name: try_on
tools.description: Get a link where the signed-in person sees their own clothes on them. Pass `outfit_id` for a saved outfit (ids come from list_saved_outfits or create_saved_outfit), or `item_ids` for a look that is not saved (for example the items suggest_outfit returned, or a single item). Returns `try_on_url`: giv

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_context · Private data: get_context, add_want, record_signal · Public sink: try_on.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_context · Private data: get_context, add_want, record_signal · Public sink: try_on

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
